notes: Hand-derived before the detector ran, under the Rust token rules (identifiers $id, literals $lit, comments dropped): five-token shingles, both bodies at least eighty tokens, shared shingles at least seventy percent of the smaller body's.
exact_a / exact_b: verbatim twins, ninety tokens each, so shingles_a == shingles_b == shared (containment 1.00). Over fifty tokens and five lines, so the same pair is also a clone group.

near_a / near_b: near_b is near_a with `if values.is_empty() { return out; }` (eleven tokens) inserted after the three lets and `total = total.max(0);` (nine tokens) inserted between the first two pushes, so shingles_b - shingles_a == 20. Each insertion breaks the four windows that straddle it; a broken window is lost unless the same normalised window occurs elsewhere in the body (`$id = $id . $id (` shapes repeat), so shared is under shingles_a but the exact loss is not hand-derivable and is pinned from the first run. The longest surviving equal run is under fifty tokens, so there is no clone group.
prefix_a / prefix_b: the signature and two lets (twenty-five tokens) are shared, the bodies are a loop against a match: containment far under seventy percent, no pair.
small_a / small_b: identical but about twenty tokens, under the eighty-token floor: no pair, and under fifty tokens so no clone group either.
observed: near pair integers from the first run on 2026-09-15, pinned as a regression; a change to the token rules or the thresholds moves them and must say so.
